chose: pytest-json matching is EQUALITY with the nodeid's final function segment ([param] stripped), not substring
over: mirroring pytest -k substring semantics like the vitest path mirrors -t
because: -k 'test_foo' also runs test_foo_extended, so a claim's evidence would depend on unrelated tests sharing a prefix; the function name is the unit a pytest claim names, and equality makes one claim buy exactly that function's parametrized cases

chose: pytest derivation is a targeted REFUSAL with setup instructions, not a derived batch command
over: deriving pytest --json-report --json-report-file=... from config.test when the command contains pytest
because: the command alone cannot prove pytest-json-report is installed (a derived command would crash into the serial fallback on every plugin-less project), and batch matching (function-name equality) is not a verified mirror of -k substring semantics — the same reason node:test is refused. Recognition without guessing: detectRunner knows pytest and deriveBatchCommand prints the exact testBatch/testBatchFormat to set

chose: pytest outcomes: failed/error/xpassed RED a match; skipped/xfailed stay NEUTRAL (no positive evidence alone, but a passing sibling case still greens the claim)
over: treating xpassed as a pass (pytest's default non-strict exit behaviour)
strict all-cases-must-be-passed (which would red a passed+skipped parametrized mix)
because: the vitest path has no leniency for anything but literal 'passed', so xpassed gets none — a passing xfail is a stale expectation, exactly what xfail_strict reds; and skipped-neutrality mirrors the vitest sibling rule ('a passed test alongside a skipped one is GREEN') so switching a project to pytest-json cannot invent reds the runner itself never reported

chose: pytest duration = call-phase seconds × 1000; absent/null call phase stays undefined
because: the call phase is the test body — the analogue of vitest's per-assertion duration — and BatchTest documents milliseconds with 'absence is absence, never zero' as the pinned rule
